text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Pager triggered: dedicated-tenant-latency (severity: page) -- tenant=acme-corp-prod, cluster=dedicated-gpu-7, metric=p95_latency > 900ms for 3m. PagerDuty incident PD-83421 created and paged on-call.

pagerduty: Page fired -> PD-83421. Escalation: primary on-call alice.nguyen.

alice.nguyen: acked. I'm on it, pulling metrics now.

alice.nguyen: quick look: p95 jumped to ~1.25s, error rate (5xx) spiked to 6.8% over last 5m. Throughput normal. Looks like KV cache miss rate increased.

ben.smith: oncall-sre here, grabbing logs + config. Any recent deploys to dedicated-gpu-7?

carla.ops: no deploys in last 30m. Autoscaler shows pool at 100% reserved capacity. There was a scheduled burst window (customer burst enabled) but not used.

alice.nguyen: prometheus query I ran: 
```
sum(rate(redwood_inference_request_duration_seconds_bucket{tenant="acme-corp-prod",quantile="0.95"}[5m]))
```
p95 series plot shows step up at 1782100900. Also KV cache hit ratio for that tenant dropped from 92% -> 31%.

emily.ml: fyi we rolled a small quantized model variant for acme a week ago, but it's been stable. Could be cache invalidation after model swap?

ben.smith: checking runtime logs -> seeing intermittent "kv-miss fallback to disk" messages and increased GPU scheduling latency. Attaching snippet: 
```
[1782100948] warning runtime: kv-cache miss tenant=acme-corp-prod key=prefix_hash_0
[1782100952] error scheduler: attempt_enqueue failed: no_available_slots
[1782100955] info runtime: fallback execution path used
```

alice.nguyen: immediate mitigation options: 1) temporarily increase reserved pool (scale up dedicated-gpu-7 by +2 nodes), 2) enable routing to fallback region (us-west-2-dedicated), or 3) enable degrade policy to serve a smaller/batch-optimized model variant. Which do we want?

carla.ops: I can scale the pool now but it will take ~3m to provision GPUs. If we route to fallback region that will add ~120-180ms network latency but should reduce errors quickly.

dave.cs: customer impact: acme is seeing user-facing app timeouts and a support ticket just came in. They report "search spikes timeout". Severity HIGH for them. Please prioritize stable path and notify CS with ETA.

alice.nguyen: taking hybrid approach: 1) carla, please spin up +2 nodes in dedicated-gpu-7 (run rcli scale --cluster dedicated-gpu-7 --add 2 --reason "incident PD-83421"). 2) ben, prep a temporary routing policy to send 30% of traffic to us-west-2-dedicated for acme-corp-prod. 3) emily, confirm model variant health if fallback model should be different.

carla.ops: running: `rcli scale --cluster dedicated-gpu-7 --add 2 --reason "incident PD-83421"` -> request accepted, job id=job-5543. ETA ~2m30s.

ben.smith: creating a canary route now: `route-manager create --tenant acme-corp-prod --target us-west-2-dedicated --weight 30 --ttl 5m --meta temporary-failover`

ben.smith: route applied. Monitoring error rate on canary traffic.

sre-bot: autoscale: job-5543 completed successfully (2 nodes added). cluster:dedi-gpu-7 capacity=+2.

alice.nguyen: cluster nodes up. Observing p95 dropping to ~420ms on origin. 5xx down to ~1.2%. Canary in us-west showing ok.

emily.ml: model check: variant v1q-2026-02 is healthy on fallback. No known regressions. If cache warm-up is needed, we should gradually increase traffic to allow KV caches to repopulate.

alice.nguyen: good. I'll keep PD incident open until we stabilize for 30m. dave, can you send an interim note to customer: "We detected a transient issue causing increased request latency for your dedicated cluster; mitigation steps are in progress and latency is improving. We will follow up with a timeline and RCA."

dave.cs: sending now. Will update ticket with ETA 30m and invite customer to status page.

ben.smith: follow-up actions I propose: 1) open an incident ticket and assign to eng-runtime and eng-infra, 2) capture KV cache invalidation events around 1782100900, 3) run cache warmup job for acme prefix keys, 4) check quantized variant rollout history.

alice.nguyen: agreed. I'll create the incident doc: https://redwood-internal/incidents/PD-83421 (placeholder). Handing over to ben for deep-dive at 13:15 PST. I'm going offline at 13:05 but will monitor notifications. Next on-call is ben.smith — please acknowledge.

ben.smith: ack, taking over primary. I'll coordinate the postmortem.

incident-bot: PD-83421 status changed -> acknowledged by ben.smith. Assigned to eng-runtime, priority P2.

alice.nguyen: quick notes for handoff in the doc: mitigation steps performed (scale +2 nodes, apply 30% fallback routing), current status: p95 ~380-450ms, 5xx ~0.9-1.3%, customer notified. Logs and queries to include: PromQL for p95, kv-cache hit ratio, scheduler queue depth.

ben.smith: on it. I'll run a targeted cache-warmup (job: warmup-acme-178210) and correlate with GPU scheduling traces. Expect updates in ~20m.

carla.ops: filing an infra follow-up to look at autoscaler thresholds; job id infra-2371.

alice.nguyen: thanks all. marking thread resolved for my shift. If we see regression -> page me. :thumbsup:

ben.smith: thanks, handing the PD incident to investigation. Closing page for now but leaving incident ticket open.

sre-bot: PD-83421 -> status: investigating -> update_time: 1782101945

[end of thread]
